synopsis: Spondylolysis is an anatomic defect of the pars interarticularis, typically a stress reaction and then a fracture from repetitive lumbar loading in extension and rotation. When the defect is bilateral, the vertebra can translate forward on the one below it; that translation is isthmic spondylolisthesis. The two are described as a continuum. Adult prevalence estimates are 5% to 11.5% for spondylolysis and 4% to 8% for isthmic spondylolisthesis. The Meyerding grade describes the slip: 0% to 25% is grade I, 25% to 50% grade II, 50% to 75% grade III, 75% to 100% grade IV, and greater than 100% is grade V, or spondyloptosis. Most patients improve with activity restriction, physical therapy, and bracing. Others need surgery for persistent symptoms. The Wiltse-Newman classification separates isthmic, dysplastic, degenerative, post-traumatic, and pathologic slips; this article focuses on spondylolysis and isthmic spondylolisthesis in adolescents and young adults.
